name: ST7789 1.3" 240×240 IPS colour TFT (SPI, 7-pin)
description: 1.3 inch 240×240 IPS colour TFT driven by a Sitronix ST7789(VW) controller over write-only 4-wire SPI (SCL clock, SDA data, DC data/command, RES reset). Chip select is tied low on the board, so the display needs SPI mode 3 and its own SPI bus. 3.3 V supply and 3.3 V logic only. Sold as: generic 1.3" 240x240 IPS TFT LCD module ST7789 SPI with 7-pin header GND, VCC, SCL, SDA, RES, DC, BLK (no CS pin), e.g. Probots 1.3 inch 240x240 IPS TFT LCD Module ST7789 SPI, universal-solder SKU 26469, ShillehTek TFT LCD 1.3" 240x240 ST7789.
eli5: A small, bright full-colour screen that your board can draw text, shapes and pictures on using a few fast wires.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V only (ST7789 VDD max 3.3 V; no level shifting on the module)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: SPI clock (named SCL but this is SPI, not I2C); 3.3 V logic

pins.name: RES
pins.description: Reset, active low (hold low >= 10 us, then wait 120 ms)

pins.name: DC
pins.description: Data/command select: low = command, high = data

pins.name: BLK
pins.description: Backlight control; pulled up on most boards so the backlight is on when left unconnected. Drive or PWM it to dim; check your board, a few are wired active-low.

supplierQuery: 1.3 inch IPS 240x240 ST7789 SPI 7 pin module
buildNotes: 3.3 V only: power VCC from the 3V3 pin and use 3.3 V logic. A 5 V Arduino needs level shifters on SCL, SDA, RES and DC.
SCL/SDA here are SPI clock and SPI data, not I2C. Wire them to the SPI SCK and MOSI pins of your board.
There is no CS pin (it is tied low on the board): use SPI mode 3 (polarity=1, phase=1) or the screen stays black, and don't share this SPI bus with other devices.
IPS panels on these modules need display inversion on (command 0x21) to show true colours; the driver sends it.
The ST7789 has 240×320 RAM: when rotated 180° or 270° the picture starts 80 pixels in. The driver applies the offset for each rotation.
A full 240×240 frame is 115 200 bytes; draw in rows or small areas rather than one big buffer on a Pico or ESP32 without PSRAM.

driver.code:
# ST7789 / ST7789VW colour TFT controller (Sitronix), MicroPython SPI driver for the common
# 1.3" 240x240 IPS module with a 7-pin header GND VCC SCL SDA RES DC BLK (CS tied low on the board).
# From the ST7789VW datasheet V1.0:
#   4-line serial: D/CX low = command byte, high = parameter/pixel bytes, MSB first.
#   Write clock cycle >= 16 ns (max ~62 MHz). With CS tied low these modules need SPI mode 3
#   (polarity=1, phase=1), so build the bus as SPI(..., polarity=1, phase=1).
#   RESX low >= 10 us, then wait 120 ms (reset cancel) before Sleep Out.
#   SWRESET (01h): wait 5 ms, and 120 ms before SLPOUT. SLPOUT (11h): wait 120 ms before SLPIN,
#   and 5 ms before the next command.
#   COLMOD (3Ah) = 55h: 16 bit/pixel RGB565. MADCTL (36h) sets orientation. INVON (21h): IPS panels
#   on these modules need inversion on to show true colours. NORON (13h), DISPON (29h).
#   CASET (2Ah) / RASET (2Bh): start and end address, 16-bit each, MSB first. RAMWR (2Ch): pixels.
# The controller has 240x320 RAM; the 240x240 panel shows RAM rows 0-239, so rotations 180/270
# need an 80-pixel offset.
from machine import Pin
import framebuf
import time

_SWRESET = 0x01
_SLPOUT = 0x11
_NORON = 0x13
_INVON = 0x21
_DISPOFF = 0x28
_DISPON = 0x29
_CASET = 0x2A
_RASET = 0x2B
_RAMWR = 0x2C
_MADCTL = 0x36
_COLMOD = 0x3A

# rotation -> (MADCTL, x offset, y offset) for a 240x240 panel on 240x320 RAM
_ROT = ((0x00, 0, 0), (0x60, 0, 0), (0xC0, 0, 80), (0xA0, 80, 0))

BLACK = 0x0000
WHITE = 0xFFFF
RED = 0xF800
GREEN = 0x07E0
BLUE = 0x001F
YELLOW = 0xFFE0


def color565(r, g, b):
    return ((r & 0xF8) << 8) | ((g & 0xFC) << 3) | (b >> 3)


class ST7789:
    def __init__(self, spi, dc, rst=None, cs=None, blk=None, width=240, height=240, rotation=0):
        # spi: machine.SPI built with polarity=1, phase=1 for the CS-less 7-pin module.
        # dc, rst, cs, blk: GPIO numbers (cs/blk None when not wired).
        self.spi = spi
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.dc = Pin(dc, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.rst = Pin(rst, Pin.OUT, value=1) if rst is not None else None
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1) if cs is not None else None
        self.blk = Pin(blk, Pin.OUT, value=1) if blk is not None else None
        self._xo = 0
        self._yo = 0
        self.reset()
        self._cmd(_SWRESET)
        time.sleep_ms(150)          # 5 ms after SWRESET, 120 ms before SLPOUT
        self._cmd(_SLPOUT)
        time.sleep_ms(120)          # sleep out settles in 120 ms
        self._cmd(_COLMOD, b'\x55')  # 16 bit/pixel
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        self.rotation(rotation)
        self._cmd(_INVON)
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        self._cmd(_NORON)
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        self.fill(BLACK)
        self._cmd(_DISPON)
        time.sleep_ms(10)

    def reset(self):
        if self.rst is None:
            return
        self.rst(1)
        time.sleep_ms(5)
        self.rst(0)
        time.sleep_ms(1)            # >= 10 us low
        self.rst(1)
        time.sleep_ms(120)          # reset cancel time

    def _cmd(self, c, data=None):
        if self.cs:
            self.cs(0)
        self.dc(0)
        self.spi.write(bytes([c]))
        if data:
            self.dc(1)
            self.spi.write(data)
        if self.cs:
            self.cs(1)

    def _data(self, buf):
        if self.cs:
            self.cs(0)
        self.dc(1)
        self.spi.write(buf)
        if self.cs:
            self.cs(1)

    def rotation(self, r):
        mad, self._xo, self._yo = _ROT[r & 3]
        self._cmd(_MADCTL, bytes([mad]))

    def window(self, x0, y0, x1, y1):
        x0 += self._xo
        x1 += self._xo
        y0 += self._yo
        y1 += self._yo
        self._cmd(_CASET, bytes([x0 >> 8, x0 & 0xFF, x1 >> 8, x1 & 0xFF]))
        self._cmd(_RASET, bytes([y0 >> 8, y0 & 0xFF, y1 >> 8, y1 & 0xFF]))
        self._cmd(_RAMWR)

    def fill_rect(self, x, y, w, h, color):
        if w <= 0 or h <= 0:
            return
        self.window(x, y, x + w - 1, y + h - 1)
        line = bytes([color >> 8, color & 0xFF]) * w
        for _ in range(h):          # one row at a time keeps RAM use small
            self._data(line)

    def fill(self, color):
        self.fill_rect(0, 0, self.width, self.height, color)

    def pixel(self, x, y, color):
        self.window(x, y, x, y)
        self._data(bytes([color >> 8, color & 0xFF]))

    def blit_buffer(self, buf, x, y, w, h):
        # buf: w*h RGB565 pixels, high byte first (the order the ST7789 expects).
        self.window(x, y, x + w - 1, y + h - 1)
        self._data(buf)

    def text(self, s, x, y, color=WHITE, background=BLACK):
        # 8x8 framebuf font. framebuf stores RGB565 little-endian, so swap the bytes of each colour
        # to get the high byte first on the wire.
        w = 8 * len(s)
        buf = bytearray(w * 8 * 2)
        fb = framebuf.FrameBuffer(buf, w, 8, framebuf.RGB565)
        sw = lambda c: ((c & 0xFF) << 8) | (c >> 8)
        fb.fill(sw(background))
        fb.text(s, 0, 0, sw(color))
        self.blit_buffer(buf, x, y, w, 8)

    def on(self):
        self._cmd(_DISPON)
        if self.blk:
            self.blk(1)

    def off(self):
        self._cmd(_DISPOFF)
        if self.blk:
            self.blk(0)

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import time
from st7789 import ST7789, WHITE, YELLOW, BLACK

# CS is tied low on this module, so it needs SPI mode 3 (polarity=1, phase=1).
spi = SPI(1, baudrate=20000000, polarity=1, phase=1, sck=Pin({SCL}), mosi=Pin({SDA}))
tft = ST7789(spi, dc={DC}, rst={RES})
tft.text('HELLO ST7789', 20, 40, WHITE, BLACK)
tft.text('240x240 IPS', 20, 60, YELLOW, BLACK)
print('drawn')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
